correctness.rationale: Connected unicyclic incidence has one-dimensional reciprocal-weight circulation cokernel; exact kernel-dimension and signed doubleton case splitting proves the formula. Exact counts of injective/single-doubleton hashes supply falling factorials, strict concavity/discrete increments prove optimizers, Weyl perturbation proves small singular values. The standalone checker matched 27 exhaustive small scenarios, 3780 exactly ranked seeded cases, and 94 optimizer comparisons; finite calculations supplement, not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: The theorem enumerates the exact probability of rank preservation for the entire weighted-unicyclic incidence family under fully independent one-sparse CountSketch, including the 0/1/1/2 collision distinctions, optimizer classifications and discontinuous weight-equality effect. The inspected general CountSketch and graph-sketch sources supply generic subspace-embedding bounds and collision avoidance, not this exact structural probability; the graph sparsification source uses a different measurement model. Related result summaries cover other graph ranks or restricted-independent hash occupancy, not this signed matrix rank event. This is bounded noncoverage evidence, not a certification of worldwide priority.
residual_risks: Searches of public indexed results and selected literature cannot prove uniqueness; equivalent treatment may appear in specialist matroid/hashed-incidence literature.
The Chen–Khanna–Li graph sparsification paper was compared by abstract only, not a full-text NOT_COVERING claim.

Graph-incidence sparse-recovery literature establishes cycle-dependent algebraic properties; abstract-only reading of Zhao et al. does not rule out a related or dominating full-text statement.

value.rationale: A natural graph numerical linear algebra benchmark asks whether sparse signed hashing preserves the nearly-full-rank incidence column space and how the sole cycle dependency changes collision tolerance. The exact success probability, its cycle-length optima, and the discontinuity in algebraic versus stable rank answer this specific design question beyond standard birthday-collision bounds. It identifies graph and weight dependence at fixed dimension and bucket budget, without promising faster general algorithms or norm embedding bounds.
